raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Status

Ready for review.  **The develop merge has landed on this branch** (one `--no-ff` merge commit of develop at `90803d73a`, #1627 included, followed by
five follow-up commits for the rename, the per-line pins, the sink guards and the tests).  What the merge keeps from #1627, untouched: its split
combine (`_combine_kernel` with the lean group and the serial walk, its own `_combine_decode_kernel` for S_q <= 2 past 16 splits, the attention-sink
fold and the per-batch Q lengths inside the combine, the three sink entries), its Blackwell re-fit of the decode split model (the launch charge, the
per-form combine prices, its candidates), its wide-tile launch rule for the Blackwell line, the fp8 dual-KV-stream route, and its native dense binder
(the split with a sink).  What this PR adds beside it: the decode-grid combine form under its own name (`_combine_decode_grid_kernel`; body unchanged
from the measured tree), taken by the entry's `decode_grid` selector for a sink-free, unquantized fp32-partial launch inside the lean-grid bound and
otherwise leaving #1627's three-way rule in place (`DECODE_GRID_OFF` means exactly that rule, and is the entry's default); the programmatic-dependent-
launch pair on every combine form under one constexpr; the 64-column decode tile (both twins carry #1627's split-aware sink guard at their two sink
sites, nothing else); the cc 10.7 refit of the decode split model as the cc 10.7 branch of ONE `choose_decode_tile_split_kv` path (develop's row seams
stay and return the cc 10.7 row's values there); the route table with both lines' readings.

**The per-line rule.**  Each arch line keeps the combine form and the split-model pricing that were measured on it: on cc 10.7 the split-aware
decode-grid form rule and this PR's refit; on every other device (the Blackwell line, measured by #1627's author on B200 / B300, and any line the rule
was never run on) the plan pins `DECODE_GRID_OFF` and the model computes exactly what develop computes.  The pin reads the plan's device through one
seam, so the SM120 adapter (which records `compute_capability`, not `_device_cc`) builds its split plans; `use_pdl=True` with an attention sink under
a split is a typed decline at `check_support` (the sink entries carry no programmatic-dependent-launch form yet).  Pick identity was checked
mechanically: over 643 968 cc 10.7 model scenarios and 724 cc 10.7 graph-level ranked lists the merged tree equals the measured tree, and over 249 792
Blackwell scenarios and 300 SM100 graph-level ranked lists it equals develop (0 mismatches on both lines).

**The extension pair** was rebuilt for the merged tree (x86 and aarch64, out of tree from a source archive of the merged head) because #1627 changes
the native dense binder; every GPU record below was taken with that pair and attests the tree, the head and the binary.

## Summary

The gated attention block's DECODE form and the standalone Rubin d256 decode graph get four levers, each a declaration knob with a readback and
each measured on a 212-SM Rubin part against vLLM main's decode chain in the same process: (1) the fused norm + RoPE projection is LOWERED to the
unfused chain at decode row counts (`fuse_norm_rope_small_m`), (2) a DECODE-GRID form of the split combine for small grids (flat in the split
count), (3) a 64-COLUMN width of the Rubin decode tile that takes a packed MTP step of up to 64 rows in ONE token unit (where two 32-column units
streamed the KV twice), and (4) programmatic dependent launch over the chain, per stage (`use_pdl`).  On top of them the decode split model is
REFIT to the measured per-width stream rates, the combine's two kernel forms and the wave structure of the launch, and the DECODE route gains one
rule the measurement forced: the paged prefill tile -- one unsplit CTA per (sequence, KV head) -- is taken only where the step fills 64 CTAs.

Against vLLM main's chain (cuBLAS projections, the fused Triton norm + RoPE + gate, the paged-KV append, the TensorRT-LLM decode kernel, the sigmoid
gate, cuBLAS o_proj; CUDA-graph replay of each step) the DECODE (S_q 1) geomean over the serving cells moves from **-8.2 % (develop's
default declaration) to +19.0 % (all four levers)**, the batch-1 class from **-16.7 % to +34.6 %**.  Every kernel number below was measured on
the tree whose kernel directories are byte-identical to this head; the host-side changes that followed (the route's fill rule, the split-model
refit) change WHICH plan a cell takes, and the cells they move are listed with the measurement that moved them or the plan that will.

## What changes, by file

| area | files | change |
|---|---|---|
| the decode tile (kernel) | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm107/decode_d256_f16.py`, `.../sm100/decode_d256_f16.py` (the shared body) | the 64-column width: four 16-column softmax groups over 256 TMEM columns, 18 warps / 576 threads, 258 KiB of SMEM (264,080 B) in the oversized carveout, spill-free at ptxas's 96-register cap on the admitted forms (the spill pins compile six arms and read the register / stack / local-memory counts); the programmatic-dependent-launch sites (the wait before the first global read, the release after the prologue) behind a compile-time switch; the SM100 twin shares the body's register trims |
| the split combine (kernel) | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm100/split_combine.py` | the DECODE-GRID kernel: one block per (row, head, batch, 64-column chunk), the split axis spread over the block's eight 16-lane chains and merged once through shared memory in a fixed order -- one dependent-load round trip up to 128 splits where the lean kernel walks 16 per pass; BITWISE the lean kernel up to 16 splits, an fp32 re-association past 16 (the pinned ladder); the griddepcontrol pair on both combine kernels; `compile_ptr(decode_grid=)` selects the form |
| the route and the config | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/config_sm107.py`, `config_sm100.py`, `engines.py`, `api_dsl.py` | ONE ordered width table `D256_DECODE_SINGLE_UNIT_Q_TILES = (16, 32, 64)` and one rule per policy; the 64-column width's FORM predicate (`decode_d256_wide_tile_admits`: a packed group of two or more heads, and over a paged cache the causal / window mask) read by the adapter, the facts twins and the block alike; the facts-only admission asks whether SOME packing rides the tile; `decode_q_tile_max` (a cap on the table, refused off cc 10.7 once, at `check_support`, whatever the graph); the SM100 factory builds over its own width set |
| the split model | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/heuristics.py`, `prepared.py` | per-width, per-arch-line KV stream rates (cc 10.7: 1.0 / 1.1 / 1.65 for the 16- / 32- / 64-column tiles; the Blackwell line keeps its fit); the combine priced by the kernel form its grid takes (`decode_combine_grid_selected`: the decode-grid kernel inside the module's 128-lean-block bound from split 8 on a grid of at most 128 rows, or from split 32; the adapter pins the form); the wave term (full waves at the saturated rate, the tail wave at its own stream count), the one-wave candidates 3 / 5 / 6 / 7, a per-width CTA cost; a multi-unit route's KV stream counted once per split (its token units share the range); past the regime the wave term was measured in, the previous pricing's pick is kept (see "What is measured, what is kept") |
| the block | `python/cudnn/gated_attention_block/api.py`, `__init__.py`, `kernels/qk_norm_rope_tma.py` | `decode_route(geometry, S_q, policy=, max_q_tile=, batch=)` and `DecodeRoute` (the kernel, width, token units, KV streams, policy, cap, `pdl_capable`, `batch` -- all readbacks); the knobs `decode_route_policy` (`single_unit` default / `token_units`), `decode_q_tile_max`, `use_pdl` (per stage: `pdl_stages`, `use_pdl_effective`), `fuse_norm_rope_small_m` (and `fuse_cache_write=True` keeping the fork under the automatic lowering; the explicit contradiction a typed decline); the served envelope `S_q <= DECODE_MAX_S_Q = DECODE_MAX_ROWS = 32` (the unpacked arm), `DECODE_PREFILL_TILE_ROWS = 128` (the prefill route's own bound, never a decline), `DECODE_PREFILL_ROUTE_MIN_CTAS = 64` (the prefill route's fill), `DECODE_CLAIMED_MAX_N_Q`; the prefill route's Q lengths as a workspace slot filled on every execute |
| docs / matrix | `docs/fe-oss-apis/gated_attention_block.md`, `python/cudnn/sdpa/frost/SUPPORT_MATRIX_TRACKER.md`, `test/python/api_index/api_index.txt` | the route tables (per group and S_q, per policy, under the cap, at and below the fill), the knob rows, the split-model paragraph; the matrix's DECODE route of record and the validated cells |
| tests | `test_block_serving_decode.py`, `test_block_serving_mtp_route.py` (new), `test_block_serving_pdl.py` (new), `test_block_serving_extend.py`, `test_sdpa_fwd_decode_d256_sm107.py`, `test_sdpa_split_combine_decode_grid.py` (new), `test_split_kv_heuristic.py`, `test_sdpa_fwd_heuristics.py`, `test_sdpa_fwd_dsl_sm107.py`, `gated_block_pdl_probe.py` (new) | the oracle matrix at every served group x S_q 1 .. 5 and the MTP cells to S_q 32 on their routes, the 64-column cells bitwise the two-unit form, the decode-grid combine's bitwise-vs-lean ladder to 16 splits and the re-association budget past it, the routing boundary and the facts twins, capture + replay of a first execute, the switch's bitwise cells and its detectors with RED twins, the split model's pins (every measured optimum, the Blackwell pins unchanged), the width / cap / fill / policy route tables |

**📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Fix the split bound in the graph ladder. It no longer matches the decode candidate ladder.**

`_graph_ladder_cells` and `_run_graph_ladder_cell` limit splits to `(kv // 128) // 2`. The docstring says this is "the candidate list's bound". That claim is now wrong. `heuristics.decode_tile_split_candidates` calls `split_kv_candidates(..., min_tiles=1)`, so the ladder goes down to one KV tile per CTA. At kv 4K (32 tiles), the ladder includes 32.

The graph ladder therefore leaves out the split that the route picks by default. `test_split_kv_heuristic.py` Line 809 pins `_decode_tile(2, 4096, combine_grid=(1, 24, 1)) == 32`, which is 32 splits of one tile each. Two parts of this file are affected:
- The L0 core cell `(1, 1, 4096, 16)` is labeled "at their route's split", but that split is not the route's pick.
- The full matrix never runs one tile per CTA through the decode-grid combine at the graph level.

Change the bound to `kv // 128`, which is `kv_tiles`. Then add `32` to the split loop, or use `decode_tile_split_candidates` directly. Also update the L0 core cell for kv 4K to split 32.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    """(B, S_q, kv, split) over B {1, 4} x S_q {1, 4} x kv {4K, 32K, 128K} x splits {4 .. 64}; a split past the candidate
-    list's bound (``kv_tiles // 2``: 16 at kv 4K) is not a plan of the graph and is left out.  ``full`` = the whole matrix
+    """(B, S_q, kv, split) over B {1, 4} x S_q {1, 4} x kv {4K, 32K, 128K} x splits {4 .. 64}; a split past the decode
+    candidate list's bound (``kv_tiles``: one KV tile per CTA, 32 at kv 4K) is not a plan of the graph and is left out.  ``full`` = the whole matrix
     (L1); otherwise the L0 core: the three B 1 x S_q 1 cells at their route's split, B 4 x kv 128K at 16, an MTP cell."""
     if not full:
-        return [(1, 1, 4096, 16), (1, 1, 32768, 32), (1, 1, 131072, 64), (4, 1, 131072, 16), (1, 4, 32768, 16)]
+        return [(1, 1, 4096, 32), (1, 1, 32768, 64), (1, 1, 131072, 64), (4, 1, 131072, 16), (1, 4, 32768, 16)]
@@
-                    if split <= (kv // 128) // 2:
+                    if split <= kv // 128:
@@
-    assert split <= (kv // 128) // 2, "a split the candidate list offers (kv_tiles // 2)"
+    assert split <= kv // 128, "a split the decode candidate list offers (kv_tiles)"
```
</details>

+def test_decode_shaped_launch_runs_the_decode_grid_kernel_and_a_prefill_shaped_one_the_lean_kernel(_m):
+    """The default entry (AUTO) picks per launch from the runtime geometry: the kernel names from the profiler."""
+    from torch.profiler import ProfilerActivity, profile

+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb

+    fn = positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(dtype_o="bf16", has_lse=True))

+        op, lp, _, _ = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+        _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits)  # warm (the first launch of a shape may carry module loads)
+        with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
+            _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits)
+        return {e.name for e in prof.events() if e.device_type.name == "CUDA" and e.name.startswith("cudnn_kernel_")}
+
+    decode = names(1, 24, 1, 256, 16)
+    prefill = names(2, 4, 1024, 256, 4)
+    assert any(n.startswith("cudnn_kernel__combine_decode_kernel") for n in decode), decode
+    assert not any(n.startswith("cudnn_kernel__combine_kernel") for n in decode), decode

+    assert not any(n.startswith("cudnn_kernel__combine_decode_kernel") for n in prefill), prefill

+# --- (2) the numerics ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

+@L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("splits", [2, 4, 5, 8, 16, 17, 20, 32, 33, 64, 65, 130], ids=lambda s: f"s{s}")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape",
+    [
+        pytest.param((1, 24, 1, 256), id="decode_b1_h24_sq1_d256", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((4, 24, 1, 256), id="decode_b4_h24_sq1_d256", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((1, 24, 4, 256), id="mtp_b1_h24_sq4_d256", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((4, 24, 4, 256), id="mtp_b4_h24_sq4_d256", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((2, 3, 5, 160), id="b2_h3_sq5_d160", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((1, 2, 1, 128), id="b1_h2_sq1_d128", marks=_gpu),
+        pytest.param((1, 2, 1, 8), id="b1_h2_sq1_d8", marks=_gpu),
+    ],
+)
+def test_decode_grid_matches_the_reference_and_is_bitwise_the_lean_kernel_up_to_sixteen_splits(shape, splits):
+    """Every form against the float64 reference (O, LSE, dead rows), two launches bitwise, AUTO == ON on these decode-shaped
+    grids, and ON == OFF bitwise for ``splits <= 16`` -- the one-chain window where the decode-grid kernel's arithmetic IS
+    the lean kernel's sequence.  Past 16 splits the two associate the sum differently (the chains' partial sums merged with
+    ``exp(m_c - m)`` factors): no bitwise claim, the reference bound only."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d = shape
+    assert comb.decode_grid_selected(b, h, sq, d)
+    fns = _entries(comb, dtype_o="bf16", has_lse=True, dtype_partial="f32")
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    outs = {}
+    for name, fn in fns.items():
+        first = _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits)
+        second = _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits)
+        assert _same(first, second), f"{name}: two launches differ (a fixed-order reduction is deterministic)"
+        _check_reference(*first, ref_o, ref_lse, sq)
+        outs[name] = first
+    assert _same(outs["auto"], outs["on"]), "a decode-shaped grid takes the decode-grid kernel under AUTO"
+    if splits <= 16:
+        assert _same(outs["on"], outs["off"]), f"splits {splits} <= 16: the decode-grid output must be bitwise the lean kernel's"
+
+
+@L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stats", ["none", "ln", "log2"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [pytest.param(torch.float16, id="f16", marks=_gpu), pytest.param(torch.bfloat16, id="bf16", marks=_gpu)])
+def test_decode_grid_stats_bases_and_output_dtypes(dtype, stats):
+    """The final LSE in both bases (the partials stay natural; the merge needs them) and the two half outputs, with and
+    without Stats, at 8 splits (bitwise the lean kernel) and 32 (the reference)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d = 1, 24, 4, 256
+    tag = "f16" if dtype == torch.float16 else "bf16"
+    fns = _entries(comb, dtype_o=tag, has_lse=stats != "none", stats_log2=stats == "log2", dtype_partial="f32")
+    for splits in (8, 32):
+        op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+        outs = {name: _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, dtype=dtype, stats=stats != "none") for name, fn in fns.items()}
+        for name in outs:
+            _check_reference(*outs[name], ref_o, ref_lse, sq, stats_log2=stats == "log2")
+        assert _same(outs["auto"], outs["on"])
+        if splits <= 16:
+            assert _same(outs["on"], outs["off"])
+
+
+@L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("_m", [pytest.param(None, marks=_gpu)])
+def test_decode_grid_strided_outputs_touch_only_their_elements(_m):
+    """The final O / Stats keep the caller's strides (Rule S5): padded storage around a strided output holds its canary
+    after the decode-grid kernel stored the row (the element-store path: a row whose storage is not 8-byte aligned or whose
+    D stride is not 1 takes it, the packed path otherwise)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d, splits = 2, 3, 5, 160, 8
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    head, token, batch = d * 2 + 8, h * (d * 2 + 8) + 16, sq * (h * (d * 2 + 8) + 16) + 32
+    ostride, lstride = (batch, token, head, 2), (h * (sq * 2 + 3) + 5, sq * 2 + 3, 2)
+
+    def storage(shape, strides, dtype):
+        span = 1 + sum((n - 1) * s for n, s in zip(shape, strides))
+        store = torch.full((span + 32,), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).to(dtype)
+        view = store.as_strided(shape, strides, storage_offset=16)
+        offsets = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.int64)
+        for axis, (n, s) in enumerate(zip(shape, strides)):
+            dims = [1] * len(shape)
+            dims[axis] = n
+            offsets += torch.arange(n).view(dims) * s
+        used = torch.zeros(store.numel(), dtype=torch.bool)
+        used[offsets.flatten() + 16] = True
+        return view, store, used
+
+    fn = positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(dtype_o="bf16", has_lse=True, decode_grid=comb.DECODE_GRID_ON))
+    o, ostore, oused = storage((b, sq, h, d), ostride, torch.bfloat16)
+    lse, lstore, lused = storage((b, h, sq), lstride, torch.float32)
+    fn(op.data_ptr(), lp.data_ptr(), o.data_ptr(), lse.data_ptr(), (b, h, sq, d), splits, ostride, lstride, torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    _check_reference(o, lse, ref_o, ref_lse, sq)
+    assert torch.all(ostore.float().cpu()[~oused] == -31.0) and torch.all(lstore.cpu()[~lused] == -31.0)
+
+
+# --- (3) the gate in the combine -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("splits", [4, 16, 64], ids=lambda s: f"s{s}")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [pytest.param(torch.bfloat16, id="bf16", marks=_gpu), pytest.param(torch.float16, id="f16", marks=_gpu)])
+def test_gate_in_combine_on_the_decode_grid(dtype, splits):
+    """The gated entry on the decode grid: ``O = merged_fp32 * sigmoid(G)`` rounded once (the reference gates its float64
+    merge; the approximate tanh and the single rounding sit inside the suite tolerance), the dead row exactly 0 under a NaN
+    gate (the SELECT after the fma, never a multiply by zero), and bitwise the lean kernel's gated output at <= 16 splits."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d = 1, 24, 4, 256
+    tag = "f16" if dtype == torch.float16 else "bf16"
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7 + splits)
+    gate = (torch.randn(b, sq, h, d, generator=gen) * 3.0).to(dtype)
+    gate[:, 0] = torch.nan  # row 0 is the all-dead row: a NaN gate there must never reach the output
+    gate = gate.cuda()
+    ref = ref_o * torch.sigmoid(gate.float().cpu().double()).masked_fill(torch.isnan(gate.float().cpu()), 0.0)
+    fns = _entries(comb, dtype_o=tag, has_lse=True, dtype_partial="f32", gate=True, dtype_gate=tag)
+    outs = {}
+    for name, fn in fns.items():
+        o, lse = _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, dtype=dtype, extra=(gate.data_ptr(), gate.stride()))
+        assert not torch.isnan(o.float()).any()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(o.cpu().float(), ref.float(), atol=0.004, rtol=0.004)
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(o[:, 0]).item() == 0, "the dead row is exactly 0 whatever G holds"
+        live = torch.isfinite(ref_lse)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(lse.cpu().double()[live], ref_lse[live], atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)  # the LSE never sees the gate
+        outs[name] = (o, lse)
+    assert _same(outs["auto"], outs["on"])
+    if splits <= 16:
+        assert _same(outs["on"], outs["off"])
+
+
+# --- (4) the ragged-Q placement ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("splits", [4, 32], ids=lambda s: f"s{s}")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("i64", [pytest.param(False, id="i32", marks=_gpu), pytest.param(True, id="i64", marks=_gpu)])
+def test_ragged_placement_on_the_decode_grid(i64, splits):
+    """The ragged-Q decode leg's entry: three sequences of 2 / 0 / 1 query rows (``S_q`` max 2) land on the packed O / Stats
+    at their offsets (tokens 0, 1 and 2; the zero-length sequence writes nothing), the rows past a sequence's length are not
+    written, a canary past the capacity is untouched, the values match the reference, and ON == OFF bitwise at <= 16 splits."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d = 3, 4, 2, 256
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    off_t = torch.int64 if i64 else torch.int32
+    q_lens = [2, 0, 1]
+    tok_off = [0, 2, 2, 3]  # exclusive prefix sums
+    # Q / O offsets in ELEMENTS of a [T, H, D] packed buffer (div = H * D), Stats offsets in elements of [H, T] per
+    # sequence (div = H: the head-major packed Stats), all int32 / int64.
+    rq = torch.tensor([t * h * d for t in tok_off], dtype=off_t, device="cuda")
+    ro = rq.clone()
+    rl = torch.tensor([t * h for t in tok_off], dtype=off_t, device="cuda")
+    cap = tok_off[-1]
+    fns = _entries(comb, dtype_o="bf16", has_lse=True, dtype_partial="f32", ragged=True, ragged_i64=i64)
+    outs = {}
+    for name, fn in fns.items():
+        o = torch.full((1, cap + 2, h, d), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)  # two canary tokens past the capacity
+        lse = torch.full((1, h, cap + 2), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+        fn(
+            op.data_ptr(),
+            lp.data_ptr(),
+            o.data_ptr(),
+            lse.data_ptr(),
+            (b, h, sq, d),
+            splits,
+            o.stride(),
+            lse.stride(),
+            rq.data_ptr(),
+            ro.data_ptr(),
+            rl.data_ptr(),
+            (h * d, h * d, h),
+            (cap, cap),
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        got_o = o[0, :cap].cpu().float()  # [T, H, D]
+        got_l = lse[0, :, :cap].cpu().double()  # [H, T]
+        want_o = torch.cat([ref_o[bi, : q_lens[bi]] for bi in range(b)], dim=0).float()
+        want_l = torch.cat([ref_lse[bi, :, : q_lens[bi]] for bi in range(b)], dim=1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got_o, want_o, atol=0.004, rtol=0.004)
+        live = torch.isfinite(want_l)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got_l[live], want_l[live], atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
+        assert torch.all(torch.isneginf(got_l[~live]))
+        assert torch.all(o[0, cap:].float() == -31.0) and torch.all(lse[0, :, cap:] == -31.0), "nothing past the capacity"
+        outs[name] = (o, lse)
+    assert _same(outs["auto"], outs["on"])
+    if splits <= 16:
+        assert _same(outs["on"], outs["off"])
+
+
+# --- (5) the graph path: the serving decode cells at every split of the route's ladder ---------------------------
+
+
+def _graph_ladder_cells(full):
+    """(B, S_q, kv, split) over B {1, 4} x S_q {1, 4} x kv {4K, 32K, 128K} x splits {4 .. 64}; a split past the candidate
+    list's bound (``kv_tiles // 2``: 16 at kv 4K) is not a plan of the graph and is left out.  ``full`` = the whole matrix
+    (L1); otherwise the L0 core: the three B 1 x S_q 1 cells at their route's split, B 4 x kv 128K at 16, an MTP cell."""
+    if not full:
+        return [(1, 1, 4096, 16), (1, 1, 32768, 32), (1, 1, 131072, 64), (4, 1, 131072, 16), (1, 4, 32768, 16)]
+    cells = []
+    for B in (1, 4):
+        for s_q in (1, 4):
+            for kv in (4096, 32768, 131072):
+                for split in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64):
+                    if split <= (kv // 128) // 2:
+                        cells.append((B, s_q, kv, split))
+    return cells

detail.body:
## Status

Ready for review.  **The develop merge has landed on this branch** (one `--no-ff` merge commit of develop at `90803d73a`, #1627 included, followed by
five follow-up commits for the rename, the per-line pins, the sink guards and the tests).  What the merge keeps from #1627, untouched: its split
combine (`_combine_kernel` with the lean group and the serial walk, its own `_combine_decode_kernel` for S_q <= 2 past 16 splits, the attention-sink
fold and the per-batch Q lengths inside the combine, the three sink entries), its Blackwell re-fit of the decode split model (the launch charge, the
per-form combine prices, its candidates), its wide-tile launch rule for the Blackwell line, the fp8 dual-KV-stream route, and its native dense binder
(the split with a sink).  What this PR adds beside it: the decode-grid combine form under its own name (`_combine_decode_grid_kernel`; body unchanged
from the measured tree), taken by the entry's `decode_grid` selector for a sink-free, unquantized fp32-partial launch inside the lean-grid bound and
otherwise leaving #1627's three-way rule in place (`DECODE_GRID_OFF` means exactly that rule, and is the entry's default); the programmatic-dependent-
launch pair on every combine form under one constexpr; the 64-column decode tile (both twins carry #1627's split-aware sink guard at their two sink
sites, nothing else); the cc 10.7 refit of the decode split model as the cc 10.7 branch of ONE `choose_decode_tile_split_kv` path (develop's row seams
stay and return the cc 10.7 row's values there); the route table with both lines' readings.

**The per-line rule.**  Each arch line keeps the combine form and the split-model pricing that were measured on it: on cc 10.7 the split-aware
decode-grid form rule and this PR's refit; on every other device (the Blackwell line, measured by #1627's author on B200 / B300, and any line the rule
was never run on) the plan pins `DECODE_GRID_OFF` and the model computes exactly what develop computes.  The pin reads the plan's device through one
seam, so the SM120 adapter (which records `compute_capability`, not `_device_cc`) builds its split plans; `use_pdl=True` with an attention sink under
a split is a typed decline at `check_support` (the sink entries carry no programmatic-dependent-launch form yet).  Pick identity was checked
mechanically: over 643 968 cc 10.7 model scenarios and 724 cc 10.7 graph-level ranked lists the merged tree equals the measured tree, and over 249 792
Blackwell scenarios and 300 SM100 graph-level ranked lists it equals develop (0 mismatches on both lines).

**The extension pair** was rebuilt for the merged tree (x86 and aarch64, out of tree from a source archive of the merged head) because #1627 changes
the native dense binder; every GPU record below was taken with that pair and attests the tree, the head and the binary.

## Summary

The gated attention block's DECODE form and the standalone Rubin d256 decode graph get four levers, each a declaration knob with a readback and
each measured on a 212-SM Rubin part against vLLM main's decode chain in the same process: (1) the fused norm + RoPE projection is LOWERED to the
unfused chain at decode row counts (`fuse_norm_rope_small_m`), (2) a DECODE-GRID form of the split combine for small grids (flat in the split
count), (3) a 64-COLUMN width of the Rubin decode tile that takes a packed MTP step of up to 64 rows in ONE token unit (where two 32-column units
streamed the KV twice), and (4) programmatic dependent launch over the chain, per stage (`use_pdl`).  On top of them the decode split model is
REFIT to the measured per-width stream rates, the combine's two kernel forms and the wave structure of the launch, and the DECODE route gains one
rule the measurement forced: the paged prefill tile -- one unsplit CTA per (sequence, KV head) -- is taken only where the step fills 64 CTAs.

Against vLLM main's chain (cuBLAS projections, the fused Triton norm + RoPE + gate, the paged-KV append, the TensorRT-LLM decode kernel, the sigmoid
gate, cuBLAS o_proj; CUDA-graph replay of each step) the DECODE (S_q 1) geomean over the serving cells moves from **-8.2 % (develop's
default declaration) to +19.0 % (all four levers)**, the batch-1 class from **-16.7 % to +34.6 %**.  Every kernel number below was measured on
the tree whose kernel directories are byte-identical to this head; the host-side changes that followed (the route's fill rule, the split-model
refit) change WHICH plan a cell takes, and the cells they move are listed with the measurement that moved them or the plan that will.

## What changes, by file

| area | files | change |

| the split combine (kernel) | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/kernels/sm100/split_combine.py` | the DECODE-GRID kernel: one block per (row, head, batch, 64-column chunk), the split axis spread over the block's eight 16-lane chains and merged once through shared memory in a fixed order -- one dependent-load round trip up to 128 splits where the lean kernel walks 16 per pass; BITWISE the lean kernel up to 16 splits, an fp32 re-association past 16 (the pinned ladder); the griddepcontrol pair on both combine kernels; `compile_ptr(decode_grid=)` selects the form |
| the route and the config | `python/cudnn/sdpa/fwd/config_sm107.py`, `config_sm100.py`, `engines.py`, `api_dsl.py` | ONE ordered width table `D256_DECODE_SINGLE_UNIT_Q_TILES = (16, 32, 64)` and one rule per policy; the 64-column width's FORM predicate (`decode_d256_wide_tile_admits`: a packed group of two or more heads, and over a paged cache the causal / window mask) read by the adapter, the facts twins and the block alike; the facts-only admission asks whether SOME packing rides the tile; `decode_q_tile_max` (a cap on the table, refused off cc 10.7 once, at `check_support`, whatever the graph); the SM100 factory builds over its own width set |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""The programmatic-dependent-launch (PDL) probes of the gated-block suite -- ONE copy, shared by the PDL test modules.
+
+``delayed_write``: a PRIMARY kernel that releases its dependent grid at once (``griddepcontrol.launch_dependents`` as its first
+instruction), spins ``spin_us`` on ``%globaltimer`` and only THEN copies ``src`` over ``dst``.  A kernel launched right after it
+with the PDL attribute may start during the spin; one that waits on its dependent grid (``griddepcontrol.wait``) before its first
+read of ``dst`` sees the copy, one that reads ``dst`` earlier sees whatever the caller left there (the tests leave NaN).  That is
+the detector of a late or missing wait: GREEN with the shipped kernel, RED with its wait removed (``retrace``).
+
+``retrace``: forget the in-process compiled objects (the compiled-plan memo and the kernel modules' ``lru_cache``d ``compile``
+entries) so the next ``compile()`` traces the kernel body again -- the way a test swaps a module-level primitive (the wait) for a
+no-op under ``monkeypatch`` and gets a kernel WITHOUT it; the caller disables the on-disk compiled-plan cache for the same reason
+(``CUDNN_FRONTEND_DISABLE_COMPILED_CACHE=1``: the cache key hashes the template FILE and the compile arguments, not the live module
+globals, so a swapped primitive would otherwise reload the shipped artifact).  Call it again after the swap is undone: the memo
+would otherwise hand the no-wait object to the next plan with the same key.
+
+``cuda_versions``: the driver / runtime / torch / DSL versions a capture test records (programmatic edges in a captured graph are a
+driver feature; the record names what served the run).
+"""
+
+import importlib.metadata
+
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import torch
+
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.barrier import launch_dependent_grids
+
+THREADS = 256
+_compiled = {}
+_FAKE_STREAM = None
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_test_delayed_write(mSrc: cute.Tensor, mDst: cute.Tensor, n: cutlass.Int32, spin_ns: cutlass.Int64) -> None:
+    # Release the dependent grid FIRST: a dependent launched with the attribute may now start.  A correct dependent still waits
+    # on this grid's completion before its first dependent read; an incorrect one reads dst before the copy below lands.
+    launch_dependent_grids()
+    t0 = cute.arch.globaltimer()
+    while cute.arch.globaltimer() - t0 < spin_ns:
+        pass
+    src = cutlass.make_array_view(mSrc)
+    dst = cutlass.make_array_view(mDst)
+    tid = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.block_idx()[0]) * cutlass.Int32(THREADS) + cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.thread_idx()[0])
+    stride = cutlass.Int32(cute.arch.grid_dim()[0]) * cutlass.Int32(THREADS)
+    for i in cutlass.range(tid, n, stride, unroll=1):
+        dst[i] = src[i]
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def delayed_write_launch(src: cute.Tensor, dst: cute.Tensor, n: cutlass.Int32, spin_ns: cutlass.Int64, n_blocks: cutlass.Int32, stream: cuda.CUstream):
+    # An ORDINARY launch (no PDL attribute): the primary of the probe is never itself a dependent of what ran before it.
+    frost_test_delayed_write(src, dst, n, spin_ns).launch(grid=(n_blocks, 1, 1), block=(THREADS, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+
+
+frost_test_delayed_write.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+def _compiled_delayed_write():
+    global _FAKE_STREAM
+    if "delayed_write" not in _compiled:
+        if _FAKE_STREAM is None:
+            from cutlass.cute.runtime import make_fake_stream
+
+            _FAKE_STREAM = make_fake_stream(use_tvm_ffi_env_stream=False)
+        fake = lambda: cute.runtime.make_fake_tensor(dtype=cutlass.Int32, shape=(cute.sym_int(),), stride=(1,), assumed_align=16)  # noqa: E731
+        _compiled["delayed_write"] = cute.compile(
+            delayed_write_launch, fake(), fake(), cutlass.Int32(0), cutlass.Int64(0), cutlass.Int32(1), _FAKE_STREAM, options="--enable-tvm-ffi"
+        )
+    return _compiled["delayed_write"]
+
+
+def _as_i32(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if not t.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError("delayed_write takes contiguous buffers (the whole slab, a whole pool), not a strided band")
+    if t.dtype == torch.int32:
+        return t
+    flat = t.view(-1)
+    if (flat.numel() * flat.element_size()) % 4:
+        raise ValueError("delayed_write copies 4-byte words; the buffer's byte count must be a multiple of 4")
+    return flat.view(torch.int32)
+
+
+def delayed_write(src: torch.Tensor, dst: torch.Tensor, *, spin_us: float, stream=None) -> None:
+    """Enqueue the primary: ``dst[:] = src`` after ``spin_us`` microseconds, the dependent grid released at once (see the module docstring).
+    ``src`` / ``dst`` are CUDA buffers of one shape and dtype (any dtype whose byte count is a multiple of 4), contiguous."""
+    if src.shape != dst.shape or src.dtype != dst.dtype or not (src.is_cuda and dst.is_cuda):
+        raise ValueError("delayed_write: src and dst must be CUDA buffers of one shape and dtype")
+    s, d = _as_i32(src), _as_i32(dst)
+    n = int(s.numel())
+    n_blocks = max(1, min(64, (n + THREADS - 1) // THREADS))  # a few CTAs: the primary must never crowd the dependent off the SMs
+    stream = torch.cuda.current_stream(src.device).cuda_stream if stream is None else stream
+    _compiled_delayed_write()(s, d, cutlass.Int32(n), cutlass.Int64(int(spin_us * 1000)), cutlass.Int32(n_blocks), cuda.CUstream(int(stream)))
+
+
+def retrace(*lru_compiles) -> None:
+    """Forget every in-process compiled object: the compiled-plan memo and the given kernel modules' ``lru_cache``d ``compile`` entries."""
+    from cudnn.frost import compiled_cache
+
+    compiled_cache.clear_memo()
+    for fn in lru_compiles:
+        fn.cache_clear()
+
+
+def cuda_versions() -> dict:
+    """The driver, runtime, torch and DSL versions of this process (what a capture test records beside its verdict)."""
+    from cuda.bindings import runtime as rt
+
+    err, drv = cuda.cuDriverGetVersion()
+    err2, run = rt.cudaRuntimeGetVersion()
+    try:
+        dsl = importlib.metadata.version("nvidia-cutlass-dsl")
+    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
+        dsl = "n/a"
+    return dict(driver=int(drv), runtime=int(run), torch=torch.__version__, torch_cuda=torch.version.cuda, dsl=dsl)

+def test_the_route_per_policy_at_every_served_group(group, policy):

+    token-unit / unpacked arms where it does not (and everywhere under ``token_units``); ``kv_streams`` names the KV streams per
+    (sequence, KV head); ``claimed`` is the packed DECODE tile at ``S_q <= 4`` only; the default policy is ``single_unit``."""

+def _former_route(geom, s_q, policy):
+    """The route BEFORE the table-driven rule (the (16, 32) table, i.e. ``decode_q_tile_max=32``): the packed decode tile in up to two
+    token units where the adapter's rule packs the group, else the tile UNPACKED up to 32 tokens, else not served -- re-derived from
+    the config's route functions, the way the former ``decode_route`` read them (``token_units`` is that rule verbatim; ``single_unit``
+    differs only where the prefill tile packs the group past the table)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.config_sm100 import decode_d256_q_units
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.config_sm107 import decode_d256_q_tile
+
+    g = geom.h_q // geom.h_kv
+    n_q = decode_d256_q_tile(s_q, g, paged=True, masked=True, max_q_tile=32) if g > 1 else 0
+    if n_q:
+        units = decode_d256_q_units(s_q, g, n_q)
+        return (_T, n_q, units, True, units)
+    n_q = decode_d256_q_tile(s_q, 1, paged=True, masked=True, max_q_tile=32)
+    return (_T, n_q, 1, False, g) if n_q else (None, 0, 0, False, 0)

+def test_the_prefill_routes_q_lengths_are_a_workspace_slot_not_plan_owned_memory():
+    """The paged THD leg's per-sequence Q lengths on the prefill route (the constant ``S_q`` of every sequence) are a ``[B]`` int32 slot
+    of the caller's workspace (Rule 8 recipes R2 + R4), reserved by the carve at the very END and only on that route: the layout with
+    ``decode_q_lens=0`` is byte-identical to before, a block on the decode tile reserves none, a block on the prefill tile reserves it
+    at declaration (before ``compile()``); the block holds no plan-owned device tensor for them and no first-execute flag -- the fill
+    rides every execute."""
+    import dataclasses
+
+    from cudnn.gated_attention_block.api import _WS_ALIGN, _align_up, _plan_workspace
+
+    geom, _ = _geom(16)
+    base = _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True)
+    assert base == _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True, decode_q_lens=0) and base.decode_q_lens == -1
+    lay = _plan_workspace(geom, 4, 8, torch.bfloat16, False, False, True, decode_q_lens=4)
+    assert lay.decode_q_lens == base.total_bytes and lay.decode_q_lens % _WS_ALIGN == 0, "the slot is appended, aligned"
+    assert lay.total_bytes == lay.engine_scratch == base.total_bytes + _align_up(4 * 4)
+    assert dataclasses.replace(lay, decode_q_lens=-1, total_bytes=base.total_bytes, engine_scratch=base.engine_scratch) == base
+    on, _ = _make_block(16, 32, 8)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 8 with 32 sequences (64 CTAs: the fill): the prefill tile
+    off, _ = _make_block(16, 32, 2)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 2: the decode tile
+    below, _ = _make_block(16, 4, 8)  # 32 / 2 at S_q 8 below the fill: two units of the decode tile, no slot
+    assert on.decode_route.prefill_tile and off.decode_route.decode_tile and below.decode_route.decode_tile
+    lay_on, lay_off = on._layout(), off._layout()
+    assert lay_on.decode_q_lens == lay_on.total_bytes - _align_up(32 * 4) >= 0 and lay_off.decode_q_lens == -1 and below._layout().decode_q_lens == -1

+#   unfused-auto:    slab GEMM | norm + RoPE (TMA) | write-through | decode tile | gated combine | out proj (declared unfused)

+    "fused-cachewrite": dict(fuse_norm_rope_small_m=True, fuse_cache_write=False),

+    "unfused-unsplit": dict(fuse_norm_rope=False, decode_split_kv=1),
+}

+@requires_rubin
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("decl, s_q", _CELLS, ids=[f"{n}-sq{s}" for n, s in _CELLS])
+def test_the_decode_step_is_bitwise_with_and_without_pdl(decl, s_q):
+    kw = _DECLARATIONS[decl]

+    on = _case(16, s_q, pdl=True, **kw)

+    assert on.route_readback() == off.route_readback(), (on.route_readback(), off.route_readback())

+    assert torch.equal(_bits(on.k_cache), _bits(off.k_cache)) and torch.equal(_bits(on.v_cache), _bits(off.v_cache)), "the write-through differs"

+@requires_rubin
+def test_capture_of_the_first_pdl_execute_replays_bitwise_the_eager_plain_and_pdl_chains(tmp_path):
+    """The serving stack's defaults on the PDL declaration: the FIRST execute of a fresh ``use_pdl=True`` block captured on a NEW
+    stream, no warm-up, under ``set_sync_debug_mode("error")``; the programmatic edges are captured without error, the capture
+    launches nothing, the replay is BITWISE the eager plain (``use_pdl=False``) chain and the eager PDL chain, and stays bitwise
+    over repeated replays.  The driver / runtime / torch / DSL versions are printed (the record of what served the capture)."""
+    v = cuda_versions()
+    print(f"cuda versions: {v}")
+    lens = (300, 0, 1000, 77)
+    plain = _Case(16, 2, lens, seed=23).compile()
+    ref = plain.run().clone()
+    plain.check_against_oracle(ref, what="plain eager")
+    case = _Case(16, 2, lens, seed=23, blk_kw=dict(use_pdl=True))  # fresh: never executed
+    case.blk.check_support()
+    case.blk.compile()
+    case.ws = torch.empty(case.blk.get_workspace_size(), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+    case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+    k_before = _written(case.k_cache)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    dumped = None
+    try:
+        if hasattr(graph, "enable_debug_mode"):
+            graph.enable_debug_mode()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            prev = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+            try:
+                case.execute()  # the FIRST execute of this declaration, captured: every launch carries the PDL attribute
+            finally:
+                torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(prev)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.isnan(case.out).all() and _written(case.k_cache) == k_before, "the capture launched work"
+        if hasattr(graph, "debug_dump"):
+            # Best effort: the graph's DOT (cudaGraphDebugDotPrint) -- the kernel-node census beside the verdict.
+            try:
+                path = str(tmp_path / "pdl_decode_graph.dot")
+                graph.debug_dump(path)
+                dot = open(path).read()
+                dumped = dict(kernel_nodes=dot.count("KERNEL"), programmatic=sum(dot.lower().count(w) for w in ("programmatic", "port")))
+            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- the dump is a record, never the verdict
+                dumped = f"debug_dump unavailable ({type(exc).__name__})"
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        replayed = case.out.clone()
+        case.check_against_oracle(replayed, what="replay")
+        assert torch.equal(replayed, ref), "the replay of the captured PDL chain differs from the eager plain chain"
+        case.out.fill_(float("nan"))
+        case.execute()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(case.out, replayed), "the eager PDL chain differs from its replay"
+        for _ in range(50):
+            graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(case.out, replayed), "repeated replays of the PDL chain are not bitwise (a race across the programmatic edges)"
+    finally:
+        graph.reset()
+    print(f"graph census: {dumped}")

+def _standalone_tile(case, *, pdl):
+    """The block's stage (4) as a standalone adapter on the block's OWN views (the decode module's ``_adapter_like``), with the switch."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl import SdpaFwdDslSm100
+
+    blk, g = case.blk, case.geom
+    q, gate_v, o, _ = case.slab_views()
+    o_buf = torch.empty_like(o)
+    bts = tuple(int(x) for x in blk._descs["block_table"].stride)
+    api = SdpaFwdDslSm100(
+        sample_q=q.transpose(1, 2),
+        sample_k=case.k_cache,
+        sample_v=case.v_cache,
+        sample_o=o_buf.transpose(1, 2),
+        sample_lse=None,
+        is_causal=g.is_causal,
+        causal_bottom_right=g.causal_bottom_right,
+        scale_softmax=g.scale,
+        seq_kv_lens_present=True,
+        sched_policy=blk._sdpa._impl.sched_policy,
+        split_kv=blk.decode_split_kv,
+        pack_gqa=True if blk.decode_route.pack_gqa else None,
+        paged_page_size=case.page,
+        paged_max_seq_len_kv=case.max_kv_len,
+        paged_table_stride=bts,
+        paged_table_v_stride=bts,
+        sample_gate=gate_v.transpose(1, 2),
+        use_pdl=pdl,
+    )
+    api.check_support()
+    api.compile()
+    assert api.kernel_template == DECODE_TILE and api.use_pdl is pdl
+    ws = torch.empty(max(api.scratch_workspace_bytes(), 1), dtype=torch.uint8, device=_DEV)
+
+    def run():
+        api.execute(
+            q.transpose(1, 2),
+            case.k_cache,
+            case.v_cache,
+            o_buf.transpose(1, 2),
+            seq_kv_lens=case.kv_lens_t,
+            block_table=case.block_table,
+            workspace=ws,
+            gate=gate_v.transpose(1, 2),
+        )
+        return o_buf
+
+    return api, run, o_buf
+
+
+_SPIN_US = (300.0, 3000.0)  # the primary's late write: well past any launch latency, so a tile that does not wait reads the NaN
+
+
+def _race_the_tile(case, run, o_buf, ref):
+    """Ahead of each tile launch: NaN over the operand, then the primary that releases its dependent at once and restores the
+    operand late.  Returns, per (operand, spin), whether the tile's output equals ``ref``."""
+    verdicts = {}
+    slab = _slab(case)
+    slab_saved = slab.clone()
+    k_saved = case.k_cache.clone()
+    for spin in _SPIN_US:
+        slab.fill_(float("nan"))
+        delayed_write(slab_saved, slab, spin_us=spin)
+        run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        verdicts[("slab", spin)] = torch.equal(o_buf, ref)
+        slab.copy_(slab_saved)
+        case.k_cache.fill_(float("nan"))
+        delayed_write(k_saved, case.k_cache, spin_us=spin)
+        run()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        verdicts[("k_pool", spin)] = torch.equal(o_buf, ref)
+        case.k_cache.copy_(k_saved)
+    return verdicts
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_detector_the_decode_tile_reads_the_slab_and_the_pools_only_after_its_dependent_wait():
+    """GREEN: the shipped tile, launched with the attribute right after a primary that released it at once and wrote the slab
+    (the Q box) or the K pool late, produces the undisturbed output -- its first read of either sits below its wait."""
+    case = _case(16, 2, pdl=True, seed=5)
+    case.run()
+    api, run, o_buf = _standalone_tile(case, pdl=True)
+    ref = run().clone()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    _, _, o_blk, _ = case.slab_views()
+    assert torch.equal(ref, o_blk), "the standalone PDL tile differs from the block's own stage (4)"
+    verdicts = _race_the_tile(case, run, o_buf, ref)
+    print(f"detector (shipped tile): {verdicts}")
+    assert all(verdicts.values()), f"the tile read an operand before its dependent wait: {verdicts}"
+
+
+@requires_rubin
+def test_detector_turns_red_when_the_tile_launches_with_the_attribute_but_does_not_wait(monkeypatch):
+    """The detector's sensitivity: the same cell with the tile's wait swapped for a no-op (the launch attribute kept, the kernel
+    retraced) reads the slab / the pool during the primary's spin -- a deliberately late (here: absent) wait turns the cell RED.
+    Runs after the GREEN cell; the retrace is undone before the next test compiles."""
+    import cudnn.frost.compiled_cache as compiled_cache
+
+    case = _case(16, 2, pdl=True, seed=5)
+    case.run()
+    mod = case.blk._sdpa._impl._k_mod  # the loaded decode module (one object per template params)
+    assert mod.__name__.startswith("cudnn.frost._templates.") and hasattr(mod, "wait_on_dependent_grids")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("CUDNN_FRONTEND_DISABLE_COMPILED_CACHE", "1")  # the on-disk artifact would be the SHIPPED kernel
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "wait_on_dependent_grids", lambda: None)
+    retrace(mod.compile)
+    try:
+        api, run, o_buf = _standalone_tile(case, pdl=True)  # a fresh trace: the attribute on, the wait gone
+        ref = run().clone()  # unraced, the no-wait tile is still correct: nothing is in flight ahead of it
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        verdicts = _race_the_tile(case, run, o_buf, ref)
+        print(f"detector (tile WITHOUT its wait): {verdicts}")
+        assert not all(verdicts.values()), f"the detector did not turn red for a tile that never waits: {verdicts}"
+        assert not any(verdicts[k] for k in verdicts if k[1] == max(_SPIN_US)), f"the longest spin must turn every operand red: {verdicts}"
+        del api, run
+    finally:
+        monkeypatch.undo()
+        retrace(mod.compile)  # the memo held the no-wait object under the shipped key
+        compiled_cache.clear_memo()
+

+_COMBINE_LENS = (8192,)  # 64 KV tiles: the tile runs long enough past its early release that a combine reading the partials at once reads garbage

+# 18-warp CTA (16,384 registers per SM sub-partition over 5 warps x 32 lanes, 8-granular, from the .reqntid the DSL emits).
+# It takes the MTP step of four tokens x 12 / 16 heads (48 / 64 rows) in ONE token unit, streaming the KV range once where the
+# 32-column tile cuts it into two units.  ROUTED (the last entry of config_sm107.D256_DECODE_SINGLE_UNIT_Q_TILES): the graph-level

+# above under ``_pin_route_max_32`` (the decode_q_tile_max=32 arm).

+_SM107_DECODE_SPILL_PROBE = textwrap.dedent("""
+    import glob, os, re, subprocess, sys
+    dump, n_q, g, form, cands = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4], sys.argv[5:]
+    os.environ["CUTE_DSL_DUMP_DIR"] = dump          # read once, at the first cutlass import
+    os.environ["CUTE_DSL_KEEP"] = "cubin"            # keep the cubin, disassemble it ourselves
+    os.environ["CUTE_DSL_ARCH"] = "sm_107a"       # unconditional: an inherited value would pin the wrong target's SASS
+    os.environ["CUDNN_FRONTEND_DISABLE_COMPILED_CACHE"] = "1"  # a compiled-plan cache HIT skips ptxas and dumps no cubin
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl import _load_sm100_kernel_module
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.config_sm100 import TemplateParams
+    toks = form.split("+")
+    kw = dict(decode_q_tile=n_q, dtype_qkv=2, seq_kv_lens_present=True, pack_gqa=g > 1, qh_per_kh=g)
+    kw["split_kv"] = next((int(t[5:]) for t in toks if t.startswith("split")), 1)
+    if "paged" in toks:
+        kw.update(paged_kv=True, page_size=16)
+    if "br" in toks:
+        kw.update(bottom_right=True, window_right=0, seq_q_lens_present=True)
+    if "swa" in toks:
+        kw.update(window_left=255)  # a left window: the record's MASK_SWA bit, the other mask the width's predicate admits over pages
+    mod = _load_sm100_kernel_module((256, 256), TemplateParams(**kw), rubin=True)
+    print("MODULE", mod.N_Q, mod.CFG.SOFTMAX_WARPS, mod.CFG.THREADS_PER_CTA)
+    mod.compile(d_qk=256, d_v=256, has_lse=True, paged_hnd="hnd" in toks, **(dict(use_pdl=True) if "pdl" in toks else {}))
+    cubins = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(dump, "*.cubin")), key=os.path.getmtime)
+    if not cubins:
+        print("FAIL no cubin dumped into", dump, os.listdir(dump)); sys.exit(3)
+    nvd = None
+    for c in cands:
+        try:
+            proc = subprocess.run([c, "-c", cubins[-1]], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
+        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+            print("REJECT", c, "->", repr(exc)); continue
+        if proc.returncode == 0 and proc.stdout.strip():
+            nvd = c; print("NVDISASM", c); break
+        print("REJECT", c, "->", (proc.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [str(proc.returncode)])[-1])
+    if nvd is None:
+        print("SKIP no nvdisasm candidate decodes the cubin"); sys.exit(0)
+    sass = subprocess.run([nvd, "-c", cubins[-1]], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.splitlines()
+    print("SASS STL", sum(1 for ln in sass if "STL" in ln))
+    print("SASS LDL", sum(1 for ln in sass if "LDL" in ln))
+    print("SASS LINES", len(sass))
+    cuobj = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(nvd), "cuobjdump")
+    if os.path.isfile(cuobj):
+        res = subprocess.run([cuobj, "-res-usage", cubins[-1]], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+        regs = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"REG:(\\d+)", res)]
+        stacks = [int(m) for m in re.findall(r"STACK:(\\d+)", res)]
+        if regs:
+            print("RES REG", max(regs))
+            print("RES STACK", max(stacks))
+    """)

+def _nvdisasm_candidates():
+    cands = []
+    if os.environ.get("CUDA_PATH"):
+        cands.append(os.path.join(os.environ["CUDA_PATH"], "bin", "nvdisasm"))
+    on_path = shutil.which("nvdisasm")
+    if on_path:
+        cands.append(on_path)
+    return [c for c in dict.fromkeys(cands) if os.path.isfile(c) and os.access(c, os.X_OK)]

+    """The 64-column tile's register budget, pinned on the SASS (no Rubin GPU: an sm_107a trace-compile in a subprocess, the
+    file's SASS-pin recipe): the 18-warp CTA's rendering stays SPILL-FREE at ptxas's 96-register cap on the admitted forms --
+    the 24/2 MTP step over HND pools, the 32/2 MTP step with split partials, a dense padded cache, and the admitted forms nearest
+    the spill edge: a packed group of TWO heads over pages (eight distinct causal thresholds per 16-column group) under the
+    bottom-right causal mask and under a left WINDOW (the predicate's other mask), plus the 24/2 step with the programmatic-
+    dependent-launch sites traced (the griddepcontrol pair must add no register pressure).  The keyed max exchange, the ftz max
+    intrinsics, the x8 O^T readbacks and the two-half epilogue of the shared body exist for this pin; a spill here is a perf
+    regression no numerics test sees (local-memory traffic in the hottest loop) -- an arm that spills is a form the config must
+    REFUSE (decode_d256_wide_tile_admits), never a silent admit.  Skips when no nvdisasm on $CUDA_PATH/bin or $PATH decodes the
+    cubin; a compile failure is a FAIL."""
+    cands = _nvdisasm_candidates()

+    out = proc.stdout.splitlines()
+    if any(ln.startswith("SKIP") for ln in out):

+    assert any(ln.startswith("MODULE 64 16 576") for ln in out), out[:5]
+    counts = {ln.split()[1]: int(ln.split()[2]) for ln in out if ln.startswith(("SASS ", "RES ")) and len(ln.split()) == 3 and ln.split()[2].isdigit()}
+    print(f"64-column tile G={g} {form}: {counts}")
+    assert counts["STL"] == 0 and counts["LDL"] == 0, f"the 64-column tile spills (G={g}, {form}): {counts}"
+    if "STACK" in counts:

+"""The shared split combine's DECODE-GRID form (``sm100/split_combine._combine_decode_grid_kernel``): one block per (row,
+head, batch, 64-column chunk) with the split axis spread over the block's eight 16-lane chains and merged once, in a fixed
+order, through SMEM -- against the module's own forms (``_combine_kernel``'s lean group and serial walk, and its decode form
+``_combine_decode_kernel`` past 16 splits at S_q <= 2) it replaces on decode-shaped grids.  ``DECODE_GRID_OFF`` is the
+module's own three-way rule: at <= 16 splits that is the lean group (``lean_wide``) or the serial walk, whose arithmetic
+is the decode-grid kernel's own sequence, so the BITWISE pins below hold against it; past 16 splits at S_q <= 2 it is the
+decode form, another fp32 association, so there the reference bound is the only claim (and what the cells assert).
+
+What this module pins: (1) the SELECTION -- the host twin ``decode_grid_selected`` reads the lean kernel's grid against
+``heuristics.DECODE_COMBINE_MAX_LEAN_BLOCKS`` (a decode step's tens of blocks take the decode-grid kernel, a prefill's
+thousands keep the module's own forms), the ``decode_grid`` keyword of ``compile_ptr`` is validated (its default is
+``DECODE_GRID_OFF``: an entry that names no form is the module's own rule on every device, and only the cc 10.7 adapter
+names AUTO), and a decode-shaped launch of the AUTO entry runs the decode-grid kernel while a prefill-shaped launch runs
+the module's lean / serial kernel (the kernel NAMES, from the profiler); (2) the NUMERICS on decode cells (B 1 / B 4, 24 Q heads, S_q 1 / 4, d 256,
+plus the suite's d 160 shape and the small head dims) at splits 2 .. 130: the float64 reference at the suite's
+tolerances, dead splits and dead rows, the LSE in both bases, two launches bitwise (every reduction is in a fixed order),
+and -- where the summation order is UNCHANGED, ``n_splits <= 16`` (only chain 0 holds splits) -- the decode-grid output
+BITWISE the OFF form's on the same inputs; past 16 splits the sum is associated differently and only the reference bound
+holds; (3) the gate-in-combine entry on the decode grid (the fp32 merged value times sigmoid(G) before the one rounding,
+the dead-row SELECT under a NaN gate, bitwise the OFF form at <= 16 splits); (4) the ragged-Q placement (packed O / Stats
+at the per-sequence offsets, a zero-length sequence, the capacity bound, int32 and int64 offsets).  Runs on any SM100-line
+part (the kernel has no arch-specific lowering; the gate entry's packed f32x2 arithmetic is Blackwell-only like the fused
+kernels'); the graph-level cells are the Rubin adapter's, which pins the form per plan (the Blackwell adapter pins OFF)."""

+def _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits, seed=20261015):
+    """Split-major partials with the suite's dead patterns: every split dead on row 0 (multi-row shapes), a dead split
+    beside live ones, the LAST split dead on head 0 (the clamped tail slots re-read it); dead payloads are NaN."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + splits)
+    o = torch.randn(splits, b, sq, h, d, generator=generator) * 0.4
+    lse = torch.randn(splits, b, h, sq, generator=generator) * 2.0 + 0.7
+    if sq > 1:
+        lse[:, :, :, 0] = -torch.inf
+    lse[1, :, :, min(1, sq - 1)] = -torch.inf
+    lse[splits - 1, :, 0, :] = -torch.inf
+    dead = torch.isneginf(lse).permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1)
+    o.masked_fill_(dead, torch.nan)
+    scores = lse.double()
+    maximum = scores.amax(0)
+    safe_maximum = torch.where(torch.isfinite(maximum), maximum, 0)
+    weights = (scores - safe_maximum).exp()
+    denominator = weights.sum(0)
+    safe_o = o.double().masked_fill(dead, 0)
+    ref_o = (weights.permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1) * safe_o).sum(0) / denominator.clamp_min(1).permute(0, 2, 1).unsqueeze(-1)
+    ref_lse = safe_maximum + denominator.log()
+    return o.reshape(splits * b, sq, h, d).cuda(), lse.reshape(splits * b, h, sq).cuda(), ref_o, ref_lse
+
+
+def _entries(comb, **kw):
+    """The three forms of one specialization: AUTO (the adapters' entry), ON and OFF (the forced kernels)."""
+    return {
+        name: positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(**kw, decode_grid=code))
+        for name, code in (("auto", comb.DECODE_GRID_AUTO), ("on", comb.DECODE_GRID_ON), ("off", comb.DECODE_GRID_OFF))
+    }
+
+
+def _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, *, dtype=torch.bfloat16, stats=True, extra=()):
+    o = torch.full((b, sq, h, d), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    lse = torch.full((b, h, sq), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) if stats else None
+    fn(
+        op.data_ptr(),
+        lp.data_ptr(),
+        o.data_ptr(),
+        lse.data_ptr() if lse is not None else None,
+        (b, h, sq, d),
+        splits,
+        o.stride(),
+        lse.stride() if lse is not None else (h * sq, sq, 1),
+        *extra,
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return o, lse
+
+
+def _check_reference(o, lse, ref_o, ref_lse, sq, *, stats_log2=False):
+    torch.testing.assert_close(o.cpu().float(), ref_o.float(), atol=0.004, rtol=0.004)
+    if sq > 1:
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(o[:, 0]).item() == 0, "the all-dead row is exactly 0"
+    if lse is not None:
+        live = torch.isfinite(ref_lse)
+        expect = ref_lse * (math.log2(math.e) if stats_log2 else 1.0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(lse.cpu().double()[live], expect[live], atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
+        assert torch.all(torch.isneginf(lse.cpu()[~live])), "a dead row's LSE is -inf"
+
+
+def _same(a, b):
+    return all((x is None and y is None) or (x is not None and y is not None and torch.equal(x, y)) for x, y in zip(a, b))
+

+def _graph_ladder_cells(full):
+    """(B, S_q, kv, split) over B {1, 4} x S_q {1, 4} x kv {4K, 32K, 128K} x splits {4 .. 64}; a split past the candidate
+    list's bound (``kv_tiles // 2``: 16 at kv 4K) is not a plan of the graph and is left out.  ``full`` = the whole matrix
+    (L1); otherwise the L0 core: the three B 1 x S_q 1 cells at their route's split, B 4 x kv 128K at 16, an MTP cell."""
+    if not full:
+        return [(1, 1, 4096, 16), (1, 1, 32768, 32), (1, 1, 131072, 64), (4, 1, 131072, 16), (1, 4, 32768, 16)]
+    cells = []
+    for B in (1, 4):
+        for s_q in (1, 4):
+            for kv in (4096, 32768, 131072):
+                for split in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64):
+                    if split <= (kv // 128) // 2:
+                        cells.append((B, s_q, kv, split))
+    return cells
+
+
+def _graph_ladder_id(c):
+    return f"b{c[0]}_sq{c[1]}_kv{c[2] // 1024}k_split{c[3]}"

**Assert the split-aware combine rule that the plan actually uses.**

`comb.decode_grid_selected(batch, 24, s_q, _D)` is the kernel module's grid-only rule. The prepared dense launch does not use that rule alone. `prepared.build_dense_spec` pins `DECODE_GRID_OFF` when `heuristics.decode_combine_force_lean(B, H_q, S_q, split)` is true. **Fix the split bound in the graph ladder. It no longer matches the decode candidate ladder.**

`_graph_ladder_cells` and `_run_graph_ladder_cell` limit splits to `(kv // 128) // 2`. The docstring says this is "the candidate list's bound". That claim is now wrong. `heuristics.decode_tile_split_candidates` calls `split_kv_candidates(..., min_tiles=1)`, so the ladder goes down to one KV tile per CTA. At kv 4K (32 tiles), the ladder includes 32.

The graph ladder therefore leaves out the split that the route picks by default. `test_split_kv_heuristic.py` Line 809 pins `_decode_tile(2, 4096, combine_grid=(1, 24, 1)) == 32`, which is 32 splits of one tile each. Two parts of this file are affected:
- The L0 core cell `(1, 1, 4096, 16)` is labeled "at their route's split", but that split is not the route's pick.
- The full matrix never runs one tile per CTA through the decode-grid combine at the graph level.

Change the bound to `kv // 128`, which is `kv_tiles`. Then add `32` to the split loop, or use `decode_tile_split_candidates` directly. Also update the L0 core cell for kv 4K to split 32.

+batch, 64-column chunk) with the split axis spread over the block's eight 16-lane chains and merged once, in a fixed order,
+through SMEM -- against the lean kernel (``_combine_kernel``) it replaces on decode-shaped grids.
+
+What this module pins: (1) the SELECTION -- the host twin ``decode_grid_selected`` reads the lean kernel's grid against
+``heuristics.DECODE_COMBINE_MAX_LEAN_BLOCKS`` (a decode step's tens of blocks take the decode-grid kernel, a prefill's
+thousands keep the lean one), the ``decode_grid`` keyword of ``compile_ptr`` is validated, and a decode-shaped launch of
+the default entry runs the decode-grid kernel while a prefill-shaped launch runs the lean kernel (the kernel NAMES, from
+the profiler); (2) the NUMERICS on decode cells (B 1 / B 4, 24 Q heads, S_q 1 / 4, d 256, plus the suite's d 160 shape
+and the small head dims) at splits 2 .. 130: the float64 reference at the suite's tolerances, dead splits and dead rows,
+the LSE in both bases, two launches bitwise (every reduction is in a fixed order), and -- where the summation order is
+UNCHANGED, ``n_splits <= 16`` (only chain 0 holds splits) -- the decode-grid output BITWISE the lean kernel's on the same
+inputs; past 16 splits the sum is associated differently and only the reference bound holds; (3) the gate-in-combine
+entry on the decode grid (the fp32 merged value times sigmoid(G) before the one rounding, the dead-row SELECT under a NaN
+gate, bitwise the lean kernel at <= 16 splits); (4) the ragged-Q placement (packed O / Stats at the per-sequence offsets,
+a zero-length sequence, the capacity bound, int32 and int64 offsets).  Runs on any SM100-line part (the kernel has no
+arch-specific lowering; the gate entry's packed f32x2 arithmetic is Blackwell-only like the fused kernels')."""
+
+import math
+
+import pytest
+
+import torch
+
+from cudnn.frost.compiled_cache import positional_entry
+
+from frost_test_utils import requires_blackwell, requires_dsl, requires_rubin
+from test_sdpa_fwd_decode_d256_sm107 import _run_graph, requires_sm107_dsl
+
+# No module-level level mark: the direct cells are L0, the full graph-level split ladder below is L1 (its core is L0).
+_gpu = [requires_dsl, requires_blackwell]
+L0 = pytest.mark.L0
+L1 = pytest.mark.L1
+
+
+def _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits, seed=20261015):
+    """Split-major partials with the suite's dead patterns: every split dead on row 0 (multi-row shapes), a dead split
+    beside live ones, the LAST split dead on head 0 (the clamped tail slots re-read it); dead payloads are NaN."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + splits)
+    o = torch.randn(splits, b, sq, h, d, generator=generator) * 0.4
+    lse = torch.randn(splits, b, h, sq, generator=generator) * 2.0 + 0.7
+    if sq > 1:
+        lse[:, :, :, 0] = -torch.inf
+    lse[1, :, :, min(1, sq - 1)] = -torch.inf
+    lse[splits - 1, :, 0, :] = -torch.inf
+    dead = torch.isneginf(lse).permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1)
+    o.masked_fill_(dead, torch.nan)
+    scores = lse.double()
+    maximum = scores.amax(0)
+    safe_maximum = torch.where(torch.isfinite(maximum), maximum, 0)
+    weights = (scores - safe_maximum).exp()
+    denominator = weights.sum(0)
+    safe_o = o.double().masked_fill(dead, 0)
+    ref_o = (weights.permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1) * safe_o).sum(0) / denominator.clamp_min(1).permute(0, 2, 1).unsqueeze(-1)
+    ref_lse = safe_maximum + denominator.log()
+    return o.reshape(splits * b, sq, h, d).cuda(), lse.reshape(splits * b, h, sq).cuda(), ref_o, ref_lse
+
+
+def _entries(comb, **kw):
+    """The three forms of one specialization: AUTO (the adapters' entry), ON and OFF (the forced kernels)."""
+    return {
+        name: positional_entry(comb.compile_ptr(**kw, decode_grid=code))
+        for name, code in (("auto", comb.DECODE_GRID_AUTO), ("on", comb.DECODE_GRID_ON), ("off", comb.DECODE_GRID_OFF))
+    }
+
+
+def _launch(fn, op, lp, b, h, sq, d, splits, *, dtype=torch.bfloat16, stats=True, extra=()):
+    o = torch.full((b, sq, h, d), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    lse = torch.full((b, h, sq), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) if stats else None
+    fn(
+        op.data_ptr(),
+        lp.data_ptr(),
+        o.data_ptr(),
+        lse.data_ptr() if lse is not None else None,
+        (b, h, sq, d),
+        splits,
+        o.stride(),
+        lse.stride() if lse is not None else (h * sq, sq, 1),
+        *extra,
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream,
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return o, lse
+
+
+def _check_reference(o, lse, ref_o, ref_lse, sq, *, stats_log2=False):
+    torch.testing.assert_close(o.cpu().float(), ref_o.float(), atol=0.004, rtol=0.004)
+    if sq > 1:
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(o[:, 0]).item() == 0, "the all-dead row is exactly 0"
+    if lse is not None:
+        live = torch.isfinite(ref_lse)
+        expect = ref_lse * (math.log2(math.e) if stats_log2 else 1.0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(lse.cpu().double()[live], expect[live], atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
+        assert torch.all(torch.isneginf(lse.cpu()[~live])), "a dead row's LSE is -inf"
+
+
+def _same(a, b):
+    return all((x is None and y is None) or (x is not None and y is not None and torch.equal(x, y)) for x, y in zip(a, b))

+    grids, and ON == OFF bitwise for ``splits <= 16`` -- the one-chain window where the decode-grid kernel's arithmetic IS
+    the lean kernel's sequence.  Past 16 splits the two associate the sum differently (the chains' partial sums merged with

+def test_decode_grid_strided_outputs_touch_only_their_elements(_m):
+    """The final O / Stats keep the caller's strides (Rule S5): padded storage around a strided output holds its canary
+    after the decode-grid kernel stored the row (the element-store path: a row whose storage is not 8-byte aligned or whose
+    D stride is not 1 takes it, the packed path otherwise)."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d, splits = 2, 3, 5, 160, 8
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    head, token, batch = d * 2 + 8, h * (d * 2 + 8) + 16, sq * (h * (d * 2 + 8) + 16) + 32
+    ostride, lstride = (batch, token, head, 2), (h * (sq * 2 + 3) + 5, sq * 2 + 3, 2)
+
+    def storage(shape, strides, dtype):
+        span = 1 + sum((n - 1) * s for n, s in zip(shape, strides))
+        store = torch.full((span + 32,), -31.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32).to(dtype)
+        view = store.as_strided(shape, strides, storage_offset=16)
+        offsets = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.int64)
+        for axis, (n, s) in enumerate(zip(shape, strides)):
+            dims = [1] * len(shape)
+            dims[axis] = n
+            offsets += torch.arange(n).view(dims) * s
+        used = torch.zeros(store.numel(), dtype=torch.bool)
+        used[offsets.flatten() + 16] = True

+def test_gate_in_combine_on_the_decode_grid(dtype, splits):
+    """The gated entry on the decode grid: ``O = merged_fp32 * sigmoid(G)`` rounded once (the reference gates its float64
+    merge; the approximate tanh and the single rounding sit inside the suite tolerance), the dead row exactly 0 under a NaN
+    gate (the SELECT after the fma, never a multiply by zero), and bitwise the lean kernel's gated output at <= 16 splits."""
+    from cudnn.sdpa.fwd.kernels.sm100 import split_combine as comb
+
+    b, h, sq, d = 1, 24, 4, 256
+    tag = "f16" if dtype == torch.float16 else "bf16"
+    op, lp, ref_o, ref_lse = _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits)
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7 + splits)

+    gate = gate.cuda()
+    ref = ref_o * torch.sigmoid(gate.float().cpu().double()).masked_fill(torch.isnan(gate.float().cpu()), 0.0)
+    fns = _entries(comb, dtype_o=tag, has_lse=True, dtype_partial="f32", gate=True, dtype_gate=tag)
+    outs = {}

+        assert not torch.isnan(o.float()).any()

+# --- (5) the graph path: the serving decode cells at every split of the route's ladder ---------------------------
+
+
+def _graph_ladder_cells(full):
+    """(B, S_q, kv, split) over B {1, 4} x S_q {1, 4} x kv {4K, 32K, 128K} x splits {4 .. 64}; a split past the candidate
+    list's bound (``kv_tiles // 2``: 16 at kv 4K) is not a plan of the graph and is left out.  ``full`` = the whole matrix
+    (L1); otherwise the L0 core: the three B 1 x S_q 1 cells at their route's split, B 4 x kv 128K at 16, an MTP cell."""
+    if not full:
+        return [(1, 1, 4096, 16), (1, 1, 32768, 32), (1, 1, 131072, 64), (4, 1, 131072, 16), (1, 4, 32768, 16)]
+    cells = []
+    for B in (1, 4):
+        for s_q in (1, 4):
+            for kv in (4096, 32768, 131072):
+                for split in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64):
+                    if split <= (kv // 128) // 2:
+                        cells.append((B, s_q, kv, split))
+    return cells
